deep.reconstruction:
The page is printed text from a German algebra textbook, probably Leiste's Arithmetik und Algebra, which Gauss owned. It has no derivation in Gauss's own hand. The handwritten fragments at the right edge are the cut-off left edge of the facing page. They match the next page's notes on the lemniscatic constant ϖ and the series K, L.

(A) End of the inheritance problem (variant 2). The estate is x and the constant is a. Child k receives k·a plus 1/n of what remains after k·a has been removed.
- Child 1 receives s1 = a + (x−a)/n = [n x + n(n−1)a]/n².
- The remainder is R1 = x − s1 = [(n−1)x − (n−1)a]/n.
- Child 2 receives s2 = 2a + (R1 − 2a)/n = [(n−1)x − (n−1)a + 2n(n−1)a]/n².
- Setting s1 = s2 and clearing the common denominator n² gives n x + n(n−1)a = (n−1)x − (n−1)a + 2n(n−1)a.
- [my step] Hence x = 2n(n−1)a − n(n−1)a − (n−1)a = n(n−1)a − (n−1)a = (n−1)²a.
- Numerical case n = 10, a = 100: x = 8100. Each share is 100 + (8100−100)/10 = 900, so there are 8100/900 = 9 children.
- [my check] In general every share equals (n−1)a, and there are n−1 children. For example R1 = 7200, s2 = 200 + 700 = 900; the last remainder is 900 = 9a, giving a share of 900 + 0.

(B) §179: solving linear systems in several unknowns by the method of equating expressions for one unknown (comparison method).
- System: x+y−z = a, x+z−y = b, y+z−x = c.
- Solve each equation for x: x = a+z−y = b+y−z = y+z−c.
- Equating the 1st and 3rd expressions gives 2y = a+c, so y = (a+c)/2.
- Equating the 2nd and 3rd gives 2z = b+c, so z = (b+c)/2.
- Then x = a + (b+c)/2 − (a+c)/2 = (a+b)/2.

(C) Facing-page fragments in Gauss's hand, visible at the right edge:
- 0, ±ϖ, ±2ϖ√−1: the lattice of lemniscatic periods.
- (1 − x⁴/ϖ⁴)…: a product expansion of the lemniscatic sine.
- Σ1/ς⁴: the lattice sum.
- ∂K/∂v, K′, vK + vvK′, (1+v)K′v + Kv: the differential relations behind Landen's transformation (1+v)K(v) = K(2√v/(1+v)).
These are fully treated on the next page.
errors: No errors in the printed mathematics. The step x = n(n−1)a − 1·(n−1)a compresses the transposition, but it is correct.

results.what: Inheritance puzzle (equal shares, child k gets k·a plus 1/n of the remainder after k·a is removed): estate x = (n−1)²a, n−1 children, each receiving (n−1)a
results.modern_name: Classical inheritance problem (linear equation / recreational algebra)
results.usually_credited_to: Traditional; Fibonacci's Liber Abaci (1202), Euler's Algebra (1770)

results.what: Solution of x+y−z=a, x+z−y=b, y+z−x=c giving x=(a+b)/2, y=(a+c)/2, z=(b+c)/2 by the comparison method
results.usually_credited_to: Standard textbook material (18th century algebra texts)

results.what: Marginal fragments (facing page) on lemniscatic periods ϖ, a product formula, Σ1/ς⁴, and differential relations for the series K, L leading to (1+v)K(v)=K(2√v/(1+v))
results.modern_name: Lemniscatic functions; Landen/Gauss transformation of complete elliptic integrals (AGM)

deep.surprise_reason: The page itself is printed routine textbook algebra. The Gauss annotations visible are only cut-off edges of facing-page notes on the lemniscate and the AGM/Landen transformation. That material is well known to be Gauss's from the Nachlass (Werke III/X).

transcription_corrections: The handwritten 'margin' at the right edge is not on page 88. It is the cut-off left edge of the facing page 89 (the 'next page'): 'Π' is Gauss's ϖ, 'V' is a fragment of √−1, and 'k, r' are K, v (e.g. '(1+r)k′+kr' = '(1+v)K′v + Kv', '∂k/∂r' = '∂K/∂v').
Printed text: 'x = n(n−1)a − 1.(n−1)a' is correctly read. The '1.' is a multiplication dot.
